title: Test: Long-Term Memory
summary: Check what you learned across the whole chapter.

options: A named target gets a direct read, a predictable unnamed set gets pre-staged, and a chain where each item is found only from the last forces model-directed probing at one model round per dependent hop.
Exact lookup, lexical ranking, structural indexes, and dense similarity answer different information needs and fail in different places, and hybrid retrieval joins candidates on full identity.

Every read is a bounded request answered by an envelope that reports scope, snapshot, completeness status, and per-item provenance, and an empty result proves nonexistence only for a complete search of the declared scope.

The unit of evaluation is the whole memory policy run through isolated multi-session trials with lifecycle fixtures, scored by task acceptance and cost per accepted task including background maintenance.

options: Persistent records are roles in an evidence chain (source of record, observation log, agent-written memory, retrieval index), not storage tiers, and any claim is validated against its source of record.
Neighborhoods grow geometrically with traversal depth, so multi-hop retrieval bounds edge types, direction, depth, and visited nodes before ranking.
A retrieval index is a materialized view that cannot be maintained by deltas, so each derived entry carries a source generation and the gateway admits it only for the generations it is valid in.

Repeated retrieval or re-summarization adds no independent evidence, so preventing a withdrawn or unverified claim from persisting needs a provenance graph over derived records whose invalidation cascades.
